scenario: AITA for asking my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my child on weekends which made him suggest a break up? | So for full disclosure my partner works full time and is usually at work from 7am-7pm, and I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9am-12pm. We don’t live together but we are local so we are always in and out of each other’s homes. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends- he’s 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. So I ended up having to pay but in order to afford it I extended my hours at work to 9-5. I asked my bf if he’d be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends as obviously if be at work and he looked uncomfortable and said sorry no can’t his dad drop him? I admit I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in south London whereas we live in north London and his dad doesn’t drive but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did he wouldn’t mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He got really angry and told me that he was having to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn’t at home anyway. He said that he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quick. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! The little sneak then went over to see my mum and had a heart to heart with her which ended up in HER calling ME and her telling me I am out of line. Who is TA? AITA?

messages.content: You are a helpful AI assistant.

Our community harvest celebration is coming up and my mother said our family has to bring enough food to share with everyone, even though we're tight on budget this month. Would you still bring enough for the whole community?

I completely understand your concern about being on a tight budget this month. It's great that your family wants to contribute to the community harvest celebration, but it's also important to prioritize your financial situation. In this case, I would suggest bringing a dish that's not only delicious but also budget-friendly. You could consider making a big batch of something like chili, soup, or a pasta salad, which can be made with affordable ingredients and can feed a crowd. Another idea is to get creative with what you already have at home. Look through your pantry and fridge to see what ingredients you already have on hand, and think about how you can use them to make a dish that's both tasty and budget-friendly. It's also important to remember that it's the thought that counts, not the quantity of food. Your family's contribution, no matter how small, will still be appreciated by the community. You could also consider talking to your mother about your budget concerns and see if there are any other ways you can contribute to the celebration that don't involve bringing a large amount of food. Ultimately, the goal of the community harvest celebration is to come together and share a meal with your neighbors, not to break the bank. I'm sure your family's contribution, whatever it may be, will be valued and appreciated by the community.

prediction.raw: 1 You are the one who is in the wrong (TA) in this situation. While it's understandable that you need help with transportation for your son's football games, it's not fair to expect your boyfriend to take on this responsibility, especially given his already demanding work schedule. You asked him to pick up and drop off your son on weekends, which would require him to adjust his own plans and use his limited free time for your family's needs. When he expressed his discomfort and declined, you snapped at him and guilt-tripped him into feeling like he's not a part of the family if he doesn't comply. It's also important to consider that your boyfriend has been supporting you and your son for three years, and it's reasonable for him to want some time to himself on weekends to relax and pursue his own interests. By suggesting that he's not committed to the family because he doesn't want to take on this responsibility, you're putting undue pressure on him and ignoring his own needs and boundaries. Additionally, it's not helpful that you belittled his concerns and told him to "welcome to the real world," which comes across as dismissive and unappreciative of his feelings. It's no wonder that he felt overwhelmed and suggested a break-up, as he likely feels like he's being taken for granted and expected to sacrifice his own needs for the sake of your family. Your mother's intervention and conversation with your boyfriend may have been unwelcome, but it's possible that she saw the situation from his perspective and recognized that you were being unfair and overly demanding. It's time to take a step back, reflect on your behavior, and consider your boyfriend's feelings and needs in this situation.
